## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `consumer-conditioned-context`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-07-24T23:56:51.483Z.

Catalog entry (23) — consumer-conditioned context shaping. Newly feasible, not a restatement of (19) task-set-conditioned scoring profiles.

Mechanism. Every context assembly today optimises for a single implicit consumer with an unknown budget. Once the acting harness is resolved from the runtime (pm-z9x1r2), the assembler knows three facts it has never had: which harness is asking, what its usable context window is, and whether the caller is a terminal human, an MCP tool call, or a piped script. Those facts condition the packer's budget, the projection depth, and the degradation order — not the relevance ranking, which stays consumer-independent.

Why it is distinct from (19). Entry (19) conditions the scoring weights on the task intent (triage, implement, review). This entry conditions the output shape on the consumer capacity. The same intent asked by a small-window harness and a large-window harness should rank identically and pack differently. Conflating the two would make relevance depend on who is asking, which is the failure mode this separation exists to prevent.

Interaction with the degradation ladder from (18). The anytime ladder decides what to drop under deadline pressure; this entry sets where the budget line sits before the ladder runs. Composition order is: intent-conditioned weights, then relevance ranking, then consumer-conditioned budget, then anytime degradation, then completeness certificate.

Small-end behaviour. At three-item scale the conditioning collapses to a no-op, because the whole workspace fits under any budget. That is the correct degeneracy and requires no special path, consistent with (21) hierarchical shrinkage serving the small end without a separate mode.

Risk to record. Consumer conditioning is a privacy-adjacent signal: the harness identity must stay local and must never be inferred from telemetry, and the hashed author context that telemetry already carries is the only form permitted to leave the machine.

Owner: this catalog. Delivery is gated on harness resolution (pm-z9x1r2) and the contract-declared output budgets (pm-5t33or) landing first. Dispositioned into the portfolio registry (pm-g8t7b9) rather than filed as a standalone item, per the catalog's standing rule that engine machinery extends the ledger.

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.
